BiblicalUsage: Abel is the second son of Adam and Eve, a keeper of sheep, and his story is the first murder in the Bible. In Genesis 4:2 he keeps the flock while Cain tills the ground, in Genesis 4:4 the Lord has respect unto Abel and his offering, and in Genesis 4:8 Cain rises up against him in the field and slays him.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Abel matters because God accepted the offering and remembered the blood: his name means breath, and his life was short, but his faith still speaks.
